summary: The catalog change that moved the fingerprint has no effect on robot_arm. bd486a2 only added washer_d1/d2/h/source to screws.M2, which the engine reads only for servo proxies with tab_washers (robot_arm has none), and changed the buy URL of shoulder_4_m3, which robot_arm does not use. kerf check --quick still passes: 0 interferences, 58 screws aligned, all non-FEA requirements ok. However, the bed-contact check added in d3677bb (12:19 UTC, after the round-9 review at 11:57) exposes a real print problem that round 9 missed. The gripper's print orientation stands it on the round bottoms of its two wrist discs. Its plates' lower edges and palm hang 11 mm above the bed on support, not on the bed as the code and DESIGN.md claim.

findings.issue: In print orientation (print_rot [90,0,0], out/parts/gripper.stl) the lowest geometry is the bottom of the two r = link_h/2 = 17 mm wrist discs. The side-plate rectangles only reach y = -6 (Rectangle(x_end, 12.0)), so the plates' 80 mm lower edges and the palm start 11 mm above the bed. Bed contact is about 36 mm2 of tessellated cylinder: two line contacts on round 7 mm discs. The largest downward flat face (897 mm2, the plate lower edges) is printed entirely on support. The engine warns 'only 0 mm2 sits on the bed against a 1669 mm2 flat face'. The gripper.py docstring ('Printed standing on its lower edges ... the jaw needs a little support') and the DESIGN.md table ('on edge, supports under the jaw') describe a print that this geometry does not make. A 37 mm tall part on two round line contacts is likely to rock, lose adhesion, or be knocked over by the nozzle. If it survives, all 80 mm of each plate edge comes off support. Every other printed part has its largest flat face on the bed (checked from the STLs).
findings.fix: Give the side plates a flat lower edge at the disc tangent. In gripper.py, extend each plate profile down to y = -r (for example Rectangle from y = -r to +6 over at least the first ~25 mm), then rise at 45 degrees back to y = -6 so the rest of the edge is self-supporting. Alternatively take the full 80 mm down to y = -r if the mass budget allows (about +12 g; arm_mass is 791 of 900 g). Then re-run kerf check (full: wrist/grip sweeps, gripper_fea, torque_wrist with the new mass). Confirm the bed-contact warning is gone, and correct the docstring and the DESIGN.md orientation row.

findings.issue: Not seen in round 9 (engine check added after it): the horn clearance holes (sh_horn on upper_arm, el_horn on forearm, wr_horn on gripper) and the cable_mast and psu_side clearance holes print horizontal without a teardrop. These are 3.4 mm clearance holes for M3, so a 0.1-0.2 mm sag at the top still passes a screw.
findings.fix: Pass teardrop=iface.print_up_deg(ctx, loc) to those horn_mount/bolt_pattern calls, as already done for the tab pilots and pivot inserts. Otherwise, add a DESIGN.md note to run a 3.4 mm drill through them.

findings.issue: Not seen in round 9: the engine warns that base_fea's fixed boxes hold none of base's fastener sites. The four 12 x 12 mm boxes do sit on the underside around the four M4 desk holes, which is the real restraint. The warning fires because those holes are cut with iface.hole and not registered as sites. The FEA setup is right, but the warning stays.
findings.fix: Cut the desk holes with a site-registering call (bolt_pattern with group 'desk') so the check can see them, or note in DESIGN.md that the boxes are the M4 desk-screw footprints.

findings.issue: Carried from round 9: DESIGN.md's Strength table gives base_fea deflection as 0.11 mm and turntable as 0.23 mm. The round-9 report values are 0.129 and 0.239. Both are under the 0.3 mm limit.
findings.fix: Update the rows to 0.13 mm and 0.24 mm.

findings.issue: Carried from round 9: upper_arm_stall_fea p99.9 is 13.34 MPa against 16 MPa (margin 1.20). The peak is at the elbow servo window frame, which is on the load path. This is the thinnest margin on the arm, and the DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.
findings.fix: Test-fit a real DS3225/DS3218 in a printed yoke_r before printing the rest (already in DESIGN.md Risks).

findings.issue: Carried over: the yaw lead routes end at base.yaw_boss, but the engine appends the servo origin as the last point, so the drawn lead ends inside the MG996R case.
findings.fix: Engine: end a lead at the servo's cable-boss point instead of its origin.

findings.issue: Carried over: kerf/electrical.py leaves the ATO fuse's cold resistance and the holder lead out of each fused run's loop resistance. The margin is still positive.
findings.fix: Engine: add the fuse cold resistance and the holder lead to each fused run.

findings.issue: Carried over: the optional 45 degree chamfer under the overhanging side of the floor tie bridge was not done.
findings.fix: Optional: chamfer the underside of the bridge block at 45 degrees.

findings.issue: Carried over: 12.6 % of the surface prints on support. Bed contact is 144 mm2 against a 465 mm2 flat face (the column is centred on the foot).
findings.fix: Optional: set the column flush with one side of the foot so that face lies on the bed.

findings.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the WAGO splices and the fuse holders sit loose on the desk.
findings.fix: None required; an electronics tray on the rear pad would be tidier.
